risks.title: Preflight smoke test previously mounted the pristine base checkpoint read-write and it was silently converted/overwritten in place
risks.impact: The one pinned parent checkpoint every future run depends on would have diverged from its recorded hash with no automatic detection until the next preflight's hash check happened to run.
risks.evidence: Live, observed during this audit's own earlier session: a first preflight recorded model.keras sha256=0da2c00a... (matches the pin); a second preflight immediately after recorded sha256=7f16e0c3... (does not match). Root cause: preflight.py's smoke test passed base_model_dir straight through as existing_model_dir to a real Docker container, which mounted it read-write and the pinned loghi-htr commit's Tokenizer.load_from_file wrote a converted tokenizer.json and a resaved model.keras back into the mounted directory.
risks.mitigation: Fixed in this session: preflight.py now calls _stage_writable_checkpoint_for_smoke_test() to copy the base checkpoint to a disposable staging directory before ever handing a path to the smoke-test runner -- the same staging discipline training_session.py already used for real runs. A regression test (test_smoke_test_never_mutates_the_real_pristine_base_checkpoint) proves the source directory is byte-identical before and after. The corrupted file was recovered from the container's own untouched model.keras.old backup and reverified against the pin.
risks.verification_method: sha256 of model.keras recomputed and matched against the pin immediately before and after two subsequent real preflight runs in this same audit session; both times unchanged.

risks.title: resume had no guard against re-entering a run already marked COMPLETED or FAILED
risks.impact: An operator (or a scripted retry) running `resume --run <a completed or failed run's directory>` would have silently re-entered orchestration, mutated a completed run's checkpoint/optimizer state again, and produced a misleading, non-final model under a run_id already declared finished.
risks.evidence: launch_guard.py's evaluate_launch_guard only rejected run_state.status in {RUNNING, STOPPING}; cli.py's own STATUS_PREPARED check in _run_session only applied when resume=False. No code path anywhere rejected `resume` on a COMPLETED or FAILED run.
risks.mitigation: Fixed in this session: evaluate_launch_guard gained an is_resume parameter and now rejects STATUS_COMPLETED/STATUS_FAILED when is_resume=True (STATUS_STOPPED remains resumable, as intended). Tests: test_resuming_a_completed_run_is_rejected, test_resuming_a_failed_run_is_rejected, test_resuming_a_stopped_run_is_allowed, test_starting_fresh_is_not_penalized_by_the_terminal_status_check.
risks.verification_method: 4 new unit tests, all passing; full_run suite 206/206, repository suite 2345 passed / 2 skipped / 0 failed after the fix.

risks.title: Launch guard never checked whether the code commit had changed since prepare, only whether the working tree was dirty
risks.impact: The exact code version that will actually execute at `start` could silently differ from the code version audited/frozen at `prepare` time, with the run's own persisted lineage metadata (code_commit_hash) falsely claiming the older commit trained the model.
risks.evidence: The run prepared earlier in this audit session (training/full-corpus-20260801T171555Z) recorded code_commit_hash=b45273f... At the time this finding was written, HEAD had already moved to 22b2f1b (a real, substantive commit: the checkpoint-mutation fix, R-001) with nothing in launch_guard.py checking for that drift.
risks.mitigation: Fixed in this session: evaluate_launch_guard gained current_code_revision and allow_code_revision_drift parameters; cli.py's _run_session now passes a freshly-read git rev-parse HEAD on every start/resume and rejects a mismatch against launch_manifest.json's frozen code_commit_hash unless explicitly overridden. A fresh run (training/full-corpus-20260801T192341Z) was re-prepared at the current HEAD (d33a32e) specifically so this audit's own evidence is internally consistent.
risks.verification_method: test_code_revision_drift_is_rejected, test_code_revision_drift_can_be_explicitly_overridden, test_matching_code_revision_is_not_flagged, and an end-to-end CLI test (test_start_rejects_code_revision_drift_since_preparation) reproducing the exact real scenario via monkeypatched git revisions.

risks.title: TrainingSessionState.global_step is never incremented anywhere in the codebase and is 0 in every real checkpoint entry
risks.impact: Every checkpoint_index.json entry's global_step field, and every dashboard/status display of it, is a permanent, uninformative placeholder rather than real state. The brief's explicit 'checkpoints must record global-step state' requirement is not met at the ArchiveTrust layer, even though the underlying optimizer likely tracks its own step count correctly inside the container.
risks.evidence: Grep of training_session.py's run_training_session shows global_step is read (CheckpointEntry.global_step=state.global_step, initial_global_step=state.global_step) but never appears on the left side of a state.model_copy(update={...}) call. Verified against real data: `python -c "...set(e['global_step'] for e in checkpoint_index.json['entries'])"` on the pilot's real 47-entry index returned {0}.
risks.mitigation: Not fixed in this audit -- requires a design decision (either surface the container's real optimizer.iterations value via a new log.csv/stdout parse, or explicitly relabel the field as 'not tracked' rather than a silently-wrong 0). Recommended before treating checkpoint metadata as a complete audit trail for a multi-day production run.
risks.verification_method: Direct source inspection (grep for global_step assignments) plus a real-data query against training/loghi-swedish-v1/run-state/checkpoint_index.json.

risks.title: The pilot's own resume-proof field 'global_step_continued_not_restarted' is computed by a check that actually re-tests epoch continuity, not global-step continuity
risks.impact: The preflight check 'optimizer_scheduler_state_serialization' (one of the 21 passing checks in this audit's own preflight run) cites this field as evidence. Because of the naming bug, the field does not actually prove what its name claims, and because global_step is always 0 (R-004), a literal global-step comparison would have been vacuously true regardless of correctness. Multi-shard optimizer-state continuity at full scale has therefore never been empirically proven -- only inferred from reading the pinned loghi-htr source (confirmed real: tf.keras.models.load_model() restores full optimizer state including its iterations counter) plus indirect behavioral evidence (the pilot's real 22-epoch validation CER improves monotonically across session/process boundaries without resetting).
risks.evidence: training_session.py::prove_full_state_resume: `global_step_continued = session_2.initial_epoch == session_1.final_epoch` -- compares epoch values, not session_2.initial_global_step / session_1.final_global_step.
risks.mitigation: Not fixed in this audit. Recommended: rename/fix the check to compare actual global_step values once R-004 is addressed, or rename the resume-proof field honestly to reflect what it currently proves (epoch continuity) and add a separate, real global-step verification once the underlying value is tracked.
risks.verification_method: Direct source inspection of prove_full_state_resume; cross-checked against the real resume-proof.json on disk.

risks.title: random_seed can silently diverge between the persisted session state and what is actually used, on resume
risks.impact: Unlike configuration_hash (which IS validated and raises ValueError on mismatch), TrainingSessionState.random_seed is only ever set once, at first creation. run_training_session accepts a fresh `random_seed` parameter on every call and uses it directly for epoch_seed computation without ever comparing it to state.random_seed or updating the persisted field. An operator supplying a different --seed on `resume` than was used at `start` (both CLI flags independently default to 42, so this requires an explicit deviation) would silently change per-shard shuffling from that point on, with the persisted random_seed field continuing to (falsely) report the original value.
risks.evidence: training_session.py::run_training_session: `elif state.configuration_hash != configuration_hash: raise ValueError(...)` exists for configuration_hash; no equivalent check exists for random_seed anywhere in the function.
risks.mitigation: Not fixed in this audit. Recommended: either validate random_seed the same way configuration_hash is validated, or remove --seed from `resume`/`start` entirely in favor of always reading it once from launch_manifest.json.
risks.verification_method: Direct source inspection of run_training_session's state-vs-parameter reconciliation logic.

risks.title: Launch guard's shard-integrity check is self-referential and only re-verifies validation overlap, never test-set overlap, at launch time
risks.impact: current_training_manifest_hash is recomputed by re-reading the same sharding_summary.json that launch_manifest.json's frozen hash was itself copied from at prepare time -- if an individual shard .parquet file were replaced or corrupted without updating that summary file, the guard would not detect it. Separately, check_train_val_overlap only rehashes/rechecks shard content against the validation manifest; the reserved test manifest is never re-verified against shard content at launch time (only at prepare time, structurally, by exclusion).
risks.evidence: launch_guard.py::_shard_line_id_overlap_with_validation only accepts a validation_manifest_path; there is no equivalent test-manifest check anywhere in evaluate_launch_guard. current_training_manifest_hash in cli.py::_run_session is read via load_sharding_summary(run_dir/'shards'), the same file build_full_corpus_shards wrote at prepare time.
risks.mitigation: Not fixed in this audit. Recommended: add a bounded, sampled or full rehash of actual shard parquet contents (not just the summary file) plus a symmetric test-manifest overlap check to the launch guard, or promote 'validate sharding' (already implemented as a separate, manual step) to a mandatory, automatic pre-launch gate.
risks.verification_method: Direct source inspection of launch_guard.py and cli.py's guard_kwargs construction.

risks.title: verify_checkpoint performs only a structural zip check, never a functional tf.keras.models.load_model() round trip, for real production checkpoints
risks.impact: A checkpoint could pass verify_checkpoint (non-empty, valid zip, no CRC errors) and still fail to functionally load for other reasons (custom-object registration, framework version mismatch, corrupted-but-structurally-valid weights), only discovered when the NEXT shard's container attempts to load it -- hours later. The failure mode itself (epoch_failed, safely handled) is already covered; the risk is wasted wall-clock time and operator confusion, not silent corruption.
risks.evidence: checkpoint_index.py::verify_checkpoint's own docstring: 'A full tf.keras.models.load_model round trip is what the resume-proof... actually exercises; this is the lightweight, always-available check.' Confirmed by reading the function body: only zipfile.testzip() plus a non-empty-file check.
risks.mitigation: Acceptable as-is for a bounded run given the existing epoch_failed handling, but the first shard/epoch review gates (Gate 4/5) should explicitly confirm at least one real resume (stop, then resume) succeeds before trusting unattended multi-day operation.
risks.owner: operator (verification step, not a code change)
risks.verification_method: Direct source inspection; recommend an explicit staged-resume test during Gate 4.

risks.title: Document-level (and possibly writer-level) leakage cannot be ruled out for 7 of 11 dataset collections
risks.impact: For single-source-file collections, pilot_split.py degrades from file-group-level splitting to line-level splitting (no true document/writer/volume identifier exists in the source data). Lines from the same physical page could legitimately appear in both train and validation/test for those specific collections, biasing validation/test CER upward (optimistic) as an estimate of true out-of-document generalization for that subset of the corpus.
risks.evidence: pilot_split.py's own module docstring and split_granularity='line_level_single_file_collection' field, disclosed per-row in the manifest -- this is a documented, not hidden, limitation. 7 of 11 collections are affected per the docstring's own count.
risks.mitigation: Disclosed, not blocking, but subgroup CER (per-collection, not just aggregate) should be computed at final evaluation (Gate 7) with this caveat explicitly stated for the affected collections; do not present aggregate CER as an unbiased estimate without this caveat.
risks.verification_method: Direct source inspection of pilot_split.py; recommend cross-checking the real pilot_split_summary.json's single_file_collections field against the full-corpus run for completeness.

risks.title: No near-duplicate (perceptual) image detection -- only exact content-hash duplicates are excluded
risks.impact: Near-identical crops (e.g. the same physical line scanned/cropped slightly differently, or minor recompression) could appear as 'unique' rows on both sides of a split boundary, silently inflating validation/test performance versus true generalization. Magnitude is unquantified because no perceptual-hash or embedding-similarity check has ever been run against this corpus.
risks.evidence: swedish_dataset_inventory.py's duplicate_status logic is keyed strictly on image_content_hash (exact byte-for-byte match) and (image_hash, transcription) pairs -- no perceptual hashing (pHash/dHash) or embedding-distance dedup exists anywhere in the codebase.
risks.mitigation: Not fixed in this audit -- would require a new, nontrivial dedup pass (perceptual hash index over 563,933 lines) and is reasonably deferred to a post-launch data-quality workstream rather than blocking this run, given exact-hash dedup already removes verbatim repeats.
risks.verification_method: Codebase-wide search for perceptual-hash/embedding-dedup logic; none found.

risks.title: Checkpoint-directory selection after a container run uses non-deterministic filesystem iteration order if more than one non-best_val .keras file is ever produced in one epoch's output
risks.impact: container_epoch_runner.py::run_epoch iterates output_root.rglob('*.keras') and unconditionally overwrites latest_dir with each non-'best_val'-named match -- 'last one wins' in arbitrary rglob order, not by name or mtime. Currently benign because the pinned container has only ever been observed to write one such file per epoch, but this is not structurally guaranteed.
risks.evidence: container_epoch_runner.py, run_epoch(): `for model_file in model_dirs: ... else: latest_dir = parent` with no sort/selection-by-name/mtime tiebreak.
risks.mitigation: Not fixed in this audit -- recommend sorting model_dirs deterministically (by epoch-directory name or mtime) before the loop as a defensive, low-risk hardening.

risks.title: TelemetrySampler's background thread has no internal exception guard beyond ImportError
risks.impact: Any unexpected exception during a _tick() call (e.g. a transient nvidia-smi or disk-usage error not already caught) would silently terminate the daemon thread with no operator-visible error. The failure degrades into the already-handled 'stale telemetry' / INTERRUPTED classification rather than crashing training, so the blast radius is bounded, but the root cause would be invisible without reading logs that do not exist for this failure.
risks.evidence: telemetry_sampler.py::TelemetrySampler._run is a bare while loop calling self._tick() with no try/except; only _query_system_sample's psutil import is guarded (ImportError only).
risks.mitigation: Not fixed in this audit -- recommend wrapping _tick() in a broad except that logs and continues, so a transient telemetry read failure doesn't quietly stop all future telemetry for the rest of a multi-day run.

risks.title: checkpoint_index.json's training_manifest_hash and validation_manifest_hash fields are always empty strings
risks.impact: A checkpoint entry cannot self-certify which manifest/shard produced it without cross-referencing configuration_hash back to training_identity.json; the fields exist on CheckpointEntry (matching the brief's explicit 'manifest identity' requirement) but are never populated by training_session.py.
risks.evidence: Real-data query against training/loghi-swedish-v1/run-state/checkpoint_index.json: `set(e.get('training_manifest_hash') for e in entries) == {''}`, same for validation_manifest_hash, across all 47 real entries.
risks.mitigation: Not fixed in this audit -- in practice epoch (=shard index) plus configuration_hash lets an auditor reconstruct manifest identity indirectly, but the dedicated fields being permanently empty is a real, disclosable gap between the schema's promise and its actual population.
risks.verification_method: Direct query against the real pilot checkpoint_index.json.

risks.title: GPU device-selection workaround treats '0' as 'all GPUs' rather than 'device 0'
risks.impact: Disclosed, intentional workaround for a real caught bug (`--gpus 0` silently allocating zero GPUs). Correct and harmless on this single-GPU host; would misbehave if a future multi-GPU host set gpu_selection='0' intending 'device 0 only'.
risks.evidence: container_epoch_runner.py::_build_argv, gpu_flag computation and its own inline comment.
risks.mitigation: Documentation note for future multi-GPU deployment; no action needed for this host/run.
risks.verification_method: Direct source inspection; nvidia-smi confirms single-GPU host.

risks.title: docker image inspect has a tight 15-second timeout that produced one transient failure during this audit
risks.impact: A real preflight run in this audit session failed the container_image_available check on a timeout, even though the image was confirmed present immediately before and after via a manual `docker image inspect`. A retry passed cleanly. This is an operational nuisance (a spurious preflight failure under load), not a correctness defect.
risks.evidence: Live preflight output in this audit session: '[FAIL] container_image_available: docker image inspect failed to run: ... timed out after 15.0 seconds', followed by a clean retry.
risks.mitigation: Consider raising the timeout modestly (e.g. 30s) or adding one internal retry for this specific check; not blocking.
risks.verification_method: Directly observed during this audit's own real preflight execution.

risks.title: The prior prepared run (training/full-corpus-20260801T171555Z) is now stale relative to current code and must not be launched as-is
risks.impact: That run's launch_manifest.json still records code_commit_hash=b45273f..., two real commits behind current HEAD (d33a32e). The newly-added R-003 guard will now correctly refuse to start or resume it without --allow-code-revision-drift. This is the intended, working behavior, not a defect -- listed here so the operator does not mistake the older run directory for the audited one.
risks.mitigation: Use training/full-corpus-20260801T192341Z (prepared at current HEAD, this audit's evidence run) for any real launch. Delete or clearly relabel the older directory to avoid operator confusion; do not launch it.
risks.verification_method: Direct comparison of the two run directories' launch_manifest.json code_commit_hash fields against `git rev-parse HEAD`.

risks.title: LR decay-per-shard behavior is architecturally sound by source-code analysis but has never been empirically measured at runtime
risks.impact: TrainingConfiguration.learning_rate_policy is recorded as 'constant_0.0001_decay_0.99'. Reading the pinned loghi-htr commit directly (.loghi-upstream/loghi-htr/src/model/optimization.py) shows this is a real, coherent exponential decay (decay_steps defaults to the single invocation's own train_batches count via decay_steps=-1, and the optimizer's step counter genuinely persists across container invocations via checkpoint reload) -- NOT a fictional label. However, this has been verified only by reading source code, not by observing real per-shard LR values at runtime, because the container's log.csv does not appear to log the learning rate.
risks.evidence: arg_parser.py: --decay_rate default 0.99, --warmup_ratio default 0.0; optimization.py::create_learning_rate_schedule and LoghiLearningRateSchedule.__call__ read directly.
risks.mitigation: Recommend Gate 4/5 explicitly check for decreasing effective step size (via loss/CER trend consistency with a decaying LR, or by adding LR to the container's logged metrics if the pinned image supports it) rather than assuming the schedule works purely from source-reading.
risks.verification_method: Direct source inspection of the pinned .loghi-upstream/loghi-htr dependency; no runtime measurement yet exists.

risks.title: No checkpoint retention policy and no mid-run disk-space monitoring; the prepared 171-shard plan needs more disk than is currently free
risks.impact: checkpoint_index.py and training_session.py never delete or prune any checkpoint directory -- every shard's 'latest' and, when it improves, 'best_val' checkpoint accumulates on disk forever. Measured real cost from the pilot's own actual run: 16GB of epoch_output for 22 epochs (du -sh training/loghi-swedish-v1/run-state/epoch_output/), i.e. ~0.727GB/epoch. Scaled to the prepared full-corpus run's 171-shard ceiling: ~124.4GB required. Current free disk on the host (D: drive): ~95.4GB (Get-PSDrive D). One full 57-shard lap over the corpus needs ~41.5GB (safely within budget), but the run would exhaust available disk space around shard ~131 (roughly 2.3 laps) if training continues that far without early stopping -- which is plausible, not guaranteed, since full-corpus convergence dynamics may differ materially from the pilot's bounded 9999-line subset. No code anywhere in training_session.py, orchestrator.py, or container_epoch_runner.py checks free disk space during the run -- disk space is checked exactly once, at preflight/launch-guard time, against a default threshold (min_free_disk_gb=20.0) that is far too low to protect against this. Disk-full failure behavior (mid-checkpoint-write, mid-shard) has never been tested.
risks.evidence: Direct measurement: `du -sh training/loghi-swedish-v1/run-state/epoch_output/` = 16G for 22 real pilot epochs. `Get-PSDrive D` free = 102466510848 bytes (~95.4GB). `grep -rn "disk_usage|disk_free|free_gb" training_session.py orchestrator.py container_epoch_runner.py` returned no matches. `grep -rn "retention|prune|delete.*checkpoint|cleanup|rmtree"` across the same files returned no matches.
risks.mitigation: Before launch: (1) either implement a bounded checkpoint retention policy (e.g. keep only 'best_val' plus the last N 'latest' checkpoints, pruning older 'latest'/'end_of_session' entries once superseded and verified-replaced) or provision materially more disk (>=150GB free recommended, giving real margin over the 124.4GB full-plan requirement), and (2) add a mid-run disk-space check that triggers a safe, checkpoint-boundary stop (mirroring the existing stop_requested()/wall-clock-budget pattern) well before exhaustion, and (3) raise preflight's default min_free_disk_gb to reflect the real per-shard cost times the configured max_full_run_epochs, not a flat 20GB. None of the three has been implemented as of this audit.
risks.owner: repository maintainer (design + implementation required before unattended multi-day operation)
risks.verification_method: Real disk measurement (du -sh) against the real pilot run directory; real free-space query against the host drive; codebase-wide search confirming no retention or mid-run disk-check logic exists.
